title: Priority inversion and intermittent deadlock in continuous batcher causing tail latency surge
creator: Asha Patel
description: Production outage window where the continuous batching subsystem repeatedly entered a blocked state under mixed-priority traffic. Small, latency-sensitive requests experienced 5–12x tail latency spikes and some requests timed out. The symptom manifested as stalled batch formation and CPU saturation on the batch coordinator followed by autoscaler churn. This ticket documents the incident timeline, root cause analysis, mitigation timeline, and the action plan (short/medium/long term).
timeline: 2026-03-09T03:12:14Z - Grafana alert: p95 latency for /v1/generate crossed 800ms (SLO 150ms)
2026-03-09T03:14:30Z - Error budget dashboard shows increased 500s from model runtime; engineers paged
2026-03-09T03:18:02Z - Initial mitigation: toggled runtime flag batch.allow_long_window=false for affected clusters (temporary reduction in throughput, immediate drop in tail latency)
2026-03-09T03:25:10Z - Observed autoscaler oscillation as throughput dipped; rolled back some aggressive scaling rules
2026-03-09T04:05:00Z - Hotfix PR opened to introduce priority-aware batching timeouts (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2451)
2026-03-09T05:12:00Z - Hotfix deployed to staging and canary; canary showed p95 back within SLO under mixed workload
2026-03-09T05:48:00Z - Hotfix promoted to prod cluster A; monitoring shows stabilization; full rollout completed by 2026-03-09T07:20:00Z
root_cause: The batch coordinator's formation logic used a coarse-grained mutex and a single FIFO queue that combined high-priority low-token requests with large long-context requests. The coordinator attempted to maximize batching throughput by waiting for batch thresholds or long-window inputs. A lock ordering issue combined with a non-preemptive batch reservation path led to priority inversion: high-priority requests were blocked waiting for workers that were themselves waiting on the coordinator to finish forming a large batch, creating a circular wait (intermittent deadlock) under certain timing patterns.
impact_summary: Incident lasted ~4 hours from detection to full rollout of the hotfix. Customer-facing effects: transient increases in token latency (p95/p99), several timed-out requests for latency-sensitive customers, and increased error rates that pushed some teams into manual failover. Internal effects: autoscaler thrashing on several clusters, on-call time and two follow-up incidents triggered by the same root pattern in different clusters.
action_items: SHORT: Add a runtime config hot-toggle (batch.priority_fastpath=true) to immediately route small/high-priority requests to a preallocated fast lane. Owner: Diego Morales, estimate 2; target: 2026-03-16
SHORT: Publish an incident runbook step to disable long-window merging in emergency. Owner: Priya Raman, estimate 1; target: 2026-03-12 (done)

MEDIUM: Refactor batch coordinator to remove coarse-grained mutex; adopt per-priority queues and non-blocking reservation protocol to eliminate circular waits. Owner: Linus Zhang, estimate 8; target: 2026-04-10
MEDIUM: Implement configurable per-priority timeouts and batch size knobs with telemetry exposures (p50/p95/p99 per priority). Owner: Morgan Lee, estimate 5; target: 2026-03-30
MEDIUM: Add unit and integration tests that reproduce priority inversion patterns (deterministic timing tests). Owner: Cameron Brooks, estimate 3; target: 2026-03-25

LONG: Introduce admission control for mixed workloads: an allocator that can reserve worker slots by priority and reject or reroute low-priority large requests when load is high. Owner: Asha Patel, estimate 13; target: 2026-Q3

LONG: Run a chaos engineering experiment that injects randomized mixing of request priorities and artificial delays to validate no deadlocks across releases. Owner: Reliability Team, estimate 5; target: 2026-Q2

OBSERVABILITY: Add a dedicated Grafana dashboard for per-priority batch metrics (formation_wait_ms, batches_formed_per_sec, queued_requests_by_priority). Owner: Diego Morales, estimate 2; target: 2026-03-18
verification_plan: Load test mixed workloads that mimic production ratios (60% long-context batchy requests, 30% short low-latency, 10% embeddings) across a range of QPS. Verify p95 and p99 for high-priority lane are within SLO under peak load and that no circular waits occur (use block-detection asserts). Canary rollout with synthetic traffic for 2 hours; monitor dashboards and error budgets before wide rollout.
notes: 03/09 Post-incident review: PM and Design invited to discuss customer impact and UI-side fallbacks. - Priya Raman attended; recommended exposing a ‘high priority’ header for customer teams.
03/11 Engineering review: Agreed to prioritize the priority_fastpath hot-toggle and per-priority metrics dashboard before refactor.
Design feedback: Consider adding a Console warning for customers when their request mix triggers admission control; link to recommended SDK flags.
Additional observation: The same pattern was observed at lower frequency in cluster C on 2026-02-27 but was not escalated; added as dependency ENG-12750 (investigate historical occurrences).
